extract:
Joni Mitchell, born Roberta Joan Anderson in Fort Macleod, Alberta, in 1943, grew up largely in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, where she survived a childhood bout of polio and taught herself ukulele and then guitar. She began performing in coffeehouses in Saskatoon and Calgary before moving to Toronto's Yorkville folk scene in the mid-1960s. A brief marriage to folk singer Chuck Mitchell took her to Detroit and gave her the surname she kept. Her recording career ran from 1968 into the 2000s, followed by a celebrated late-life return to the stage.

Her formative influences ranged from the folk revival to jazz and classical music, and she developed dozens of open guitar tunings that shaped her distinctive harmonic voice. Before she had a record of her own, her songs circulated through other singers: Tom Rush, Judy Collins and Fairport Convention recorded her material, and Collins had a hit with Both Sides Now. David Crosby saw her perform in Florida, brought her to Los Angeles, and produced her debut, Song to a Seagull (1968), for Reprise Records.

Clouds (1969) included her own version of Both Sides Now. Ladies of the Canyon (1970), rooted in the Laurel Canyon community she shared with Graham Nash and others, featured Big Yellow Taxi, The Circle Game and Woodstock, a song Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young turned into a hit. Blue (1971), spare and confessional, with songs like A Case of You, River and California, became her defining work. After moving to David Geffen's Asylum Records she released For the Roses (1972), then Court and Spark (1974), her commercial peak, backed by Tom Scott's L.A. Express and featuring Help Me and Free Man in Paris. The live Miles of Aisles (1974) captured that period.

From there she moved steadily toward jazz. The Hissing of Summer Lawns (1975) used Burundi drumming on The Jungle Line and puzzled many critics. Hejira (1976), written during cross-country travel, was built around Jaco Pastorius's fretless bass on tracks like Coyote and Amelia. Don Juan's Reckless Daughter (1977) went further still, and Mingus (1979) grew out of her collaboration with Charles Mingus, who died before its release. The live Shadows and Light (1980) featured Pastorius, Pat Metheny, Michael Brecker and Lyle Mays. In the 1980s she signed with Geffen Records and made the pop-leaning Wild Things Run Fast (1982) and the synthesizer-heavy Dog Eat Dog (1985), co-produced with Thomas Dolby. Bassist and engineer Larry Klein, her husband during this era, was a key collaborator.

Her critical standing only rose over time. Blue regularly appears near the top of all-time album rankings, and musicians including Prince, Björk and many later singer-songwriters have cited her as an influence. She was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1997, received Kennedy Center Honors, and won Grammys including for Both Sides Now (2000), her orchestral reworking of standards and her own songs.

After a brain aneurysm in 2015 left her relearning to walk and speak, Joni Mitchell made an unexpected return, performing at the 2022 Newport Folk Festival with Brandi Carlile, released as the live album Joni Mitchell at Newport, and later headlining shows at the Gorge Amphitheatre. Her archival series of reissues continues to document her early career. She is widely regarded as one of the most important songwriters of the twentieth century.
title: Joni Mitchell
